For antiretroviral therapy (ART) cohort reports, data is collected at baseline and then at intervals of 6, 12, and 24 months after initiating ART. For example, a cohort starting ART in July 2019 would have results reported in January 2020 (6 months), July 2020 (12 months), and July 2021 (24 months). This process is repeated for subsequent cohorts starting ART in different months and years. Patients are categorized based on their ART regimen: first-line, second-line (switched), or third-line (switched). Additionally, data is collected on patients who stopped treatment, died, or were lost to follow-up (LTFU). The percentage of the cohort alive and on ART is calculated using the formula [(H + I + J) / C] 100, where H, I, and J represent the number of patients on first-line, second-line, and third-line regimens, respectively, and C represents the net current cohort. Viral load (VL) testing is a critical component of monitoring ART outcomes. The number of patients on ART for at least 6 months who received a VL test result is recorded (N). Among these, the number of patients with suppressed VL (defined as <1000 copies/mL) is also recorded (O). The percentage of patients with suppressed VL is calculated as [O / N] 100. The WHO has updated the threshold for defining patients living with HIV on ART who are LTFU from 90 days to 28 days or more since the last missed appointment, including missed antiretroviral (ARV) refills in either facility or community settings. Differentiated service delivery (DSD) ART models are used to improve ART delivery. Facilities with electronic medical records (EMRs) can identify patients eligible for DSD ART models based on criteria such as being on ART for at least 6 months, having no current illness, demonstrating good adherence, and showing evidence of treatment success (e.g., suppressed VL or adequate CD4 count). The number of patients enrolled in DSD ART models is recorded, excluding those who transferred out. The percentage of eligible patients enrolled in DSD ART models is calculated as [R / Q] 100, where R represents the number of enrolled patients and Q represents the number of eligible patients. For pregnant and breastfeeding women, ART cohort analysis may require more frequent tracking, aligned with maternal and child health (MCH) visits. Data on ARV coverage for mothers of breastfeeding infants is disaggregated by pregnancy or breastfeeding status at intervals of 0, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Long-term cohort analysis is conducted at the facility level, with yearly cohort analyses being relevant. For patients on ART for five or more years, it may be practical to combine cohorts into annual ART start-up groups and track their outcomes over time (e.g., 2-, 3-, or 5-year intervals). Data from the first five years before combination may be entered retrospectively. The ART cohort analysis report records the most recent patient outcomes over the past 6, 12, or 24 months. Transfer-in and deceased patients are always counted cumulatively across columns, while transfer-out patients may return and stop being counted as transfers out once they do so. These patients remain in the original cohort and are included in the net current cohort. The ART register is used to record baseline data for each cohort at the end of the month. Subsequent columns are used to record results at 6, 12, and 24 months. At baseline, no patients are recorded as transfers in, transfers out, stopped, dead, or LTFU. These outcomes are recorded in the 6-month column and beyond. The net current cohort is calculated by adding transfers in and subtracting transfers out from the original cohort. Patients on first-line regimens are recorded in the first-line regimen column at baseline. At 6, 12, and 24 months, the number of patients still on the first-line regimen is compared to the baseline. Patients who switch to second-line or third-line regimens are recorded in their respective columns. The number of patients who stopped, died, or are LTFU is also recorded during the reporting periods. For facilities with EMRs, data on patients eligible for and enrolled in DSD ART models is extracted. The number of patients enrolled in DSD ART models who received a VL test and those with suppressed VL is recorded. ART retention among patients enrolled in DSD ART models is calculated as [X / R] 100, where X represents the number of patients retained on treatment at 12 and 24 months. In summary, ART cohort analysis involves systematic data collection and reporting at specified intervals to monitor treatment outcomes, retention, and viral suppression among patients living with HIV.
